title: Knowledge grounding: which data can a Copilot Studio agent answer from?
summary: The controls, credit rates and grounding limitations are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the changed Work IQ page does not contradict the explanation here. Minor corrections should complete the Dataverse search path, cite the source connecting its API property to search, and acknowledge Microsoft's separate restriction of included standard-harness usage to Microsoft 365 channels.

claims.claim: Knowledge sources ground Copilot Studio agent responses in enterprise content.
claims.quote: Knowledge sources ground your agent's responses in enterprise data.

claims.claim: For standard-harness agents, makers can incorporate knowledge on the agent's Knowledge page.
claims.quote: You can incorporate knowledge at the agent level, in the Knowledge page, or at the topic level, with a generative answers node in an agent topic.

claims.claim: Knowledge can be incorporated in a generative answers node inside a topic.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, you can also add knowledge sources to a generative answers topic node.

claims.claim: Published agents use their configured knowledge sources for grounding.
claims.quote: Published agents that contain knowledge use the configured knowledge sources to ground the published agent.

claims.claim: With agent user authentication, responses surface only content the asking user can access.
claims.quote: Agent user authentication for knowledge sources means that when a specific user asks a question of the agent, the agent only surfaces content that the specific user can access.

claims.claim: SharePoint, Dataverse and enterprise data with Copilot connectors require authentication configured.
claims.quote: If you're using SharePoint, Dataverse, or enterprise data with Microsoft Copilot connectors, you need to incorporate authentication.

claims.claim: Dataverse knowledge sources require Dataverse search enabled in the environment.
claims.quote: To use this knowledge source, Copilot Studio agents must use Dataverse search. If you can't add a Dataverse table to an agent, ask your administrator to turn on Dataverse search in your environment.

claims.claim: A Dataverse knowledge source can contain up to 15 tables.
claims.quote: You can add up to 15 Dataverse tables per knowledge source.

claims.claim: Dataverse table knowledge requires Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: Dataverse tables as knowledge sources require you to set your agent's authentication to Authenticate with Microsoft. The other two options, No authentication and Authenticate manually aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Generative orchestration uses an internal GPT model to filter knowledge when there are more than 25 different sources.
claims.quote: Generative orchestration filters knowledge sources by using an internal GPT model when there are more than 25 different knowledge sources.

claims.claim: Uploaded files are excluded from the 25-source search count.
claims.quote: Files uploaded to the agent aren't part of the 25 knowledge source search limit.

claims.where: What it is: A different sense
claims.claim: Work IQ enables agents to reach Microsoft 365 and business data.
claims.quote: In addition to productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications, Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, and data from connected enterprise systems through Copilot Connectors.

claims.claim: Makers choose their agents' knowledge source types.
claims.quote: Makers can choose which types of knowledge sources their agents can reference.

claims.claim: Administrators can restrict SharePoint and OneDrive, public website and document knowledge source types.
claims.quote: The Knowledge sources for agents setting in Power Platform admin center controls access to sources such as SharePoint, OneDrive, public websites, and documents such as files.

claims.claim: The administrator setting's preview page does not state its default.
claims.quote: Searched: "knowledge sources for agents" "default"; read learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/knowledge-sources-for-agents-rule and environment-groups-rules, plus microsoft-copilot-studio/choose-knowledge-sources. No default for this rule was stated.

claims.claim: Allow ungrounded responses controls whether a turn using no knowledge source or tool may answer from general knowledge.
claims.quote: When you turn on the Allow ungrounded responses setting, your agent can respond by using the model's general knowledge, even when it doesn't use any knowledge sources or tools.

claims.claim: No admin-centre setting specifically for Allow ungrounded responses is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow ungrounded responses" API PowerShell admin center setting; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "Allow ungrounded responses". Read knowledge-copilot-studio, advanced-generative-actions and FAQ search excerpts; no admin-centre equivalent found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers stay possible
claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses on, responses are not limited to configured sources.
claims.quote: The agent can then respond by using the model's general knowledge, so its answers aren't always grounded in your knowledge sources.

claims.claim: Grounded agent answers are metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.

claims.claim: The cited Billing rates and management article describes standard-harness agents.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The classic answer billing rate is 1 Copilot Credit.
claims.quote: | Classic answer | 1 Copilot Credit | No charge |

claims.claim: The generative answer billing rate is 2 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Generative answer | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding for messages costs 10 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Tenant graph grounding for messages | 10 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: Microsoft gives an example of a tenant graph grounded agent consuming 12 Copilot Credits for a complex prompt.
claims.quote: For example, an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 Copilot Credits (10 Copilot Credits for tenant graph grounding, and 2 Copilot Credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges Copilot Credits for LLM tokens.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges for tools including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges for the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: The standard-harness billing page includes employee-facing usage in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the agent user is licensed and the agent uses that authenticated user's identity.
claims.quote: are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user of the agent is licensed with Microsoft Copilot, and the agent operates using the authenticated Microsoft Copilot USL user's identity.
claims.fix: After this inclusion sentence add: 'The harness cost-management page limits standard-harness inclusion to Microsoft 365 channels and says usage in a channel outside Microsoft 365 is billed.' Cite and add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness to sources; its table says 'Yes, in Microsoft 365 channels' and 'Billed when the user has no Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or when the agent is used in a channel outside Microsoft 365.' Retain attribution of the existing statement to the billing page.

claims.claim: Included employee-facing usage is subject to fair usage limits.
claims.quote: Usage is limited to fair usage limits. Microsoft reserves the right to update the limits as the product evolves, and new usage patterns emerge.

claims.claim: The billing page says generative answers incur charges unless the agent was created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response does not use tenant graph grounding.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding is optional per agent.
claims.quote: This capability is optional, and you can turn it on or off for each agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users use tenant graph grounding semantic search by default.
claims.quote: By default, all users with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses use tenant graph grounding semantic search.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[4].governs; What to check
claims.claim: Enabling tenant graph semantic search for users without Microsoft 365 Copilot licences comes at extra cost.
claims.quote: However, if not all end users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, turn on this setting to leverage semantic index for those users to improve quality. This feature comes at an extra cost.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding requires a configured semantic index.
claims.quote: It also requires that a semantic index is configured for use.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence in the agent's tenant.
claims.quote: This feature requires the agent to share a tenant with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: At least one enterprise user must be assigned that Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to use the semantic index.
claims.quote: To use a semantic index, the Microsoft 365 Copilot license must be assigned to at least one user in the enterprise.

claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: When you use Upload files > SharePoint as a knowledge source, your files are stored in Dataverse, where they're processed and indexed for use.

claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint consume data storage.
claims.quote: Your files and folders remain in Dataverse, so they do consume data storage.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers stay possible
claims.claim: Turning Allow ungrounded responses off does not prevent general knowledge being combined with retrieved content.
claims.quote: The agent's underlying model might still incorporate general knowledge when it combines this knowledge with information it retrieves from knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses off, the agent blocks responses in turns that use no knowledge source or tool.
claims.quote: When you turn off this setting, the agent blocks any response generated in a turn where it didn't use a knowledge source or tool.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: This blocking includes follow-up answers based on conversation history without calling a source or tool.
claims.quote: This condition means the response is blocked if the agent answers a question from conversation history or general knowledge without calling a knowledge source or tool.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses off, a knowledge-source answer requires an in-text citation.
claims.quote: When you turn off Allow ungrounded responses, the agent returns an answer from a knowledge source only when the answer includes an in-text citation to that source.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: A correct knowledge-source answer without a citation is withheld when the setting is off.
claims.quote: Occasionally, the model generates a correct answer from a knowledge source but doesn't include a citation for it. When that happens, the agent withholds the answer and responds as though it didn't find any information.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The Documents setting is narrow

claims.quote: Configuring Documents knowledge source to not allow uploads only prevents local file uploads.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The Documents setting is narrow

claims.quote: It doesn't prevent makers from adding files from SharePoint or OneDrive. To not allow uploads from SharePoint or OneDrive, configure SharePoint + OneDrive to not allow access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Uploaded files skip per-user checks

claims.where: Risks and limits: Uploaded files skip per-user checks
claims.claim: SharePoint file and folder sources verify the user's permission before responding.
claims.quote: With SharePoint, the user's credentials are verified to ensure they have permission to access the file before providing responses.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off breaks sources
